newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon, Kuwait, Egypt in stock cross-trade deals.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon, Kuwait, Egypt in stock cross-trade deals.

text.p: Brokers from the Lebanese, Egyptian and Kuwait stock exchanges signed bilateral agreements on Friday under which they will start cross-trading equities at the beginning of January.

"A total of 121 bilateral cooperation agreements were signed between brokerage houses working in the three stock exchanges," Sa'faq al-Rukeibi, secretary-general of the Union of Arab Stock Exchanges, told Reuters at a meeting organised by the union.

"The share of Egyptian firms was 101 contracts, the share of Kuwaiti firms was 80 contracts and the share of Lebanese firms was 59 contracts," Rukeibi added at the end of the two-day meeting of some 80 brokers from the three markets.

The agreements effectively bypass the unresolved issue of cross-listing of shares between the three bourses. They follow agreements earlier this year between the three stock exchanges and their clearance houses.

Brokers said that under the agreements the Lebanese and Egyptian stock exchanges would be open to investors from all three countries, while investors from Egypt and Lebanon would have access at present only to investment and real-estate funds in Kuwait.

Rukeibi said Kuwaiti authorities were working on opening up their market to non-Kuwaiti investors for direct share ownership but the process needed time because it would have to be approved by the relevant government institutions.
